title: SRTP key derivation panic during cross-stack WebRTC setup
observation: rust-to-go, go-to-rust and rust-to-cinnabar fail at the initial 32-byte connection before any measured echo; the Rust process reports generic-array length assertion left 32 / right 16. The Go client reports association closed before connecting, while the preserved Rust server stderr contains the same panic. Cinnabar-to-rust and both Cinnabar/Go directions pass all four sizes.
diagnostic: A separate untimed rust-to-go run with RUST_BACKTRACE=1 reaches webrtc_srtp::key_derivation::aes_cm_key_derivation, called by CipherAeadAesGcm::new, Context::new and RTCPeerConnection::set_remote_description. It reproduces the same 32-versus-16-byte assertion. No cipher/profile restriction, dependency patch or panic suppression was applied to the measured defaults.
source_evidence: webrtc-srtp 0.14.0 src/key_derivation.rs:43-44 constructs GenericArray::from_slice(master_key) followed by Aes128::new(key); src/cipher/cipher_aead_aes_gcm.rs stores Aes128Gcm and derives keys using master_key.len(). The observed key-length mismatch identifies this dependency boundary; the negotiated SRTP profile itself was not logged.
reproduction: On logical CPUs 16-23 with TOKIO_WORKER_THREADS=8, GOMAXPROCS=8, BENCH_SPLIT_COUNT=1 and RUST_BACKTRACE=1, start go-bench nethernet-serve --address 127.0.0.1:50051 --count 1, then bench-compare nethernet-client with the same address/count. Port 50051 must be available. Server/client are independent processes with the benchmark-local JSON-string signaling bridge.
follow_up: Investigate the dependency's SRTP key derivation/profile support separately from SCTP echo stalls. This task measures and reports the gap; it does not optimize or patch production transports.
